analysis:
Examined the base-side text of .github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py (lines 1-1083) together with the head patch excerpt for lines 949-982. The patch adds three CI review-tooling tests and touches no provider code.

- test_manual_github_rerun_hands_off_without_any_paid_work: a GitHub rerun (GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=2) must make no paid calls, collect no source and produce a non-clean report.
- test_scanner_runtime_is_bounded_and_ci_can_use_fifty_minutes: the runtime defaults to 900s, accepts up to 3000s and rejects invalid values.
- test_workload_ceiling_hands_off_at_the_exact_unadmitted_stage: a Bedrock workload call ceiling stops at the unadmitted stage and requires human review.

These are offline test fixtures for the threat-review CI pipeline (budget, merge-policy and handoff behavior). They do not touch provider, coordinator, attestation, encryption or cache assets. Threats T-041, TB-002/003/007/009/011 and A-001 through A-017 are unaffected. The tests use only synthetic tokens and a local 127.0.0.1 server, and they assert fail-closed behavior: clean() is false and no spend occurs.

The referenced implementations were not supplied: threat-model-review.py runtime_seconds, the budget_runner rerun handling, the Bedrock call policy, and the bedrock_run/bedrock_response helpers. The tests assert intended fail-closed behavior but do not prove it; that is a coverage limit for integration, not a security regression in the provider threat model. No regression was identified.
